o1.biggest_strength: Every ad set gets a rupee decision built on after-RTO, Shopify-adjusted economics, and it catches all three owner signals: relaunch the paused creator video, split women 25-34, cut the COD-trap Starter Kit.
o1.biggest_mistake: The two-line 'safe ₹282 / break-even ₹394' framework double-counts the attribution gap on top of per-set RTO math and gets confusing (the Starter Kit break-even of ₹271 vs ₹194 is muddled), which risks a wrong pause/scale call.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Clean one-number break-even per ad set (no parallel safe line) with the attribution haircut applied once and shown.

o2.biggest_strength: Rigorous, traceable economics with a state-split holdout test for retargeting that genuinely answers whether retargeting pays, plus a reserve-released-by-rule budget that caps at ₹5,60,000.
o2.biggest_mistake: Dense and over-engineered for a 'I want decisions, not reporting' owner; the holdout test and multiple probability assumptions add reading load, and holding the Starter Kit's COD issue while staying at ₹60,200 on Beard Kit and ₹56,000 on UGC is debatable.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut the extra frameworks down to decisions and one clean budget table so the Monday actions jump off the page.

reason: Both catch the three signals, but Output 2's numbers trace cleanly to one break-even per ad set with a real holdout for retargeting, while Output 1's parallel safety lines risk a wrong call; Output 2 reads heavier but I trust its rupees more.
